1.title: Islamic New Year
1.description: The starting point of the Islamic calendar, established under the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab to commemorate the emigration (Hijra) of the Prophet ﷺ and the first Muslims from Mecca to Medina, the founding event of the Muslim state. Celebrated civilly and culturally in many Muslim countries.

10.title: Day of Ashura
10.description: The day Allah delivered the prophet Musa (Moses) and the Children of Israel from the tyranny of Pharaoh, who drowned in the sea; Musa fasted this day in gratitude to Allah. The Prophet ﷺ declared that the Muslims have a greater right to follow Musa. In the Sunni tradition, it is a day of gratitude and spiritual joy. In the Shia tradition, it concludes an intense period of mourning (from the 1st to the 10th of Muharram) commemorating the martyrdom of Al-Hussein ibn Ali and his companions at the battle of Karbala in 61 AH.

20.title: Arba'in
20.description: A Shia commemoration marking the fortieth day after the martyrdom of Imam Al-Hussein. It is the occasion of one of the largest religious gatherings in the world: several million pilgrims converge on foot toward the shrine of Karbala in Iraq.

9.title: Farhat az-Zahra
9.description: A popular Shia celebration marking the end of the two-month mourning period after Ashura and the beginning of the imamate of the twelfth imam.

12.title: Mawlid an-Nabawi
12.description: Commemoration of the birth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (according to the most widespread opinion). A public holiday and festive day in much of the Sunni world, marked by readings of the Prophetic biography (Sirah) and poems of praise. The attribution of a specific festive ritual to this date is a matter of juridical debate among scholars, since the notion of a liturgical festival ('Eid) is reserved, in Sunni orthodoxy, to the festivals instituted by the Prophet ﷺ.

20.title: Birth of Fatima az-Zahra
20.description: Birth of Fatima az-Zahra, daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, commemorated in the Shia tradition (Mawalid Ahl al-Bayt).

13.title: Birth of Ali ibn Abi Talib
13.description: Birth of Ali ibn Abi Talib, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ and first Imam of Shia Islam, born inside the Ka'aba according to the Shia tradition.

27.title: Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj
27.description: Commemoration of the Prophet's ﷺ miraculous journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, followed by his ascension through the heavens, the night during which the five daily prayers were instituted. The determination of the exact date is a matter of disagreement among historians.

27.title: Eid al-Mab'ath
27.description: A Shia festival celebrating the first day of the prophetic mission of Muhammad ﷺ and the beginning of the revelation.

3.title: Birth of Al-Hussein ibn Ali
3.description: Birth of Al-Hussein ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet ﷺ and third Imam of Shia Islam, commemorated in the Shia tradition (Mawalid Ahl al-Bayt).

15.title: Mid-Sha'ban
15.description: The night of the middle of Sha'ban marking the approach of the month of Ramadan; certain texts mention the descent of divine mercy and forgiveness during this night.

15.title: Birth of Imam al-Mahdi
15.description: A Shia celebration of the birth of the twelfth imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi, the awaited Imam.

15.title: Birth of Al-Hassan ibn Ali
15.description: Birth of Al-Hassan ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet ﷺ and second Imam of Shia Islam, commemorated in the Shia tradition (Mawalid Ahl al-Bayt).

21.title: Martyrdom of Ali ibn Abi Talib
21.description: A Shia commemoration of the death of Ali ibn Abi Talib, which occurred on the 21st of Ramadan after he was struck on the 17th or 19th of Ramadan, marked by nights of prayer and lamentation.

27.title: Night of Destiny
27.description: The night during which the Quran began to be revealed, and whose worth exceeds a thousand months of worship (﴾لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴿). It falls during the last ten nights of Ramadan, most particularly the odd nights (21, 23, 25, 27 and 29), the night of the 27th being the most commonly retained.

1.title: Eid al-Fitr
1.description: The canonical festival of breaking the fast, instituted in year 2 of the Hijra. Upon his arrival in Medina, the Prophet ﷺ replaced two days of entertainment inherited from the pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyyah) with two better days: the day of al-Adha and the day of al-Fitr. It celebrates the completion of the fourth pillar of Islam — the fast of the month of Ramadan — and constitutes an act of gratitude to Allah for having enabled the believers to complete this month of worship.

1.title: The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja
1.description: The period from the 1st to the 10th of Dhu al-Hijja: the most virtuous days of the year for pious deeds, encompassing the pilgrimage, the day of Arafat and the day of sacrifice.

9.title: Day of Arafat
9.description: The fundamental pillar of Hajj, during which the pilgrims stand on the plain of Arafat to implore divine forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ said of fasting on this day (for non-pilgrims) that it expiates the sins of the previous year and the following year.

10.title: Eid al-Adha
10.description: The canonical festival of sacrifice (Yawm an-Nahr), instituted in year 2 of the Hijra at the same time as Eid al-Fitr. It commemorates the trial of faith and complete submission of the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), whom Allah ordered in a dream to sacrifice his son Ismail, before substituting a beast for him as a ransom. It also marks the culmination of the great pilgrimage (Hajj), the fifth pillar of Islam, following the gathering on Mount Arafat. The three days of Tashriq (from the 11th to the 13th) extend the festival.

18.title: Eid al-Ghadir
18.description: The greatest Shia festival (al-'Aïd al-Akbar). It commemorates the event of Ghadir Khumm, on the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, where the Prophet ﷺ pronounced praises in honor of his cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom the Shia consider to have been explicitly designated by him as his successor and the first legitimate Imam.

24.title: Eid al-Mubahala
24.description: A Shia festival commemorating the mutual imprecation ordeal (Mubahala) between the Prophet ﷺ — accompanied by his close family (Ali, Fatima, Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein) — and the Christian delegation of Najran.

26.title: Day of the Cave
26.description: A commemoration temporarily instituted in the 4th century of the Hijra (Abbasid era) to celebrate the entry of the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr into the cave of Thawr during the Hijra, in response to the Shia Eid al-Ghadir.
